paragraphs.source_en: Beginning with Elizabeth Gaskell’s Life of Charlotte Brontë (1857), innumerable accounts of the lives and the world of the Brontës have been published—so many that the family has acquired legendary status. Myths about the Brontës have also circulated widely, and much recent scholarship has been devoted to sorting fact from fiction. The two biographies noted below are even-handed studies, while the collection of letters enables the Brontës to speak in their own voices. Emily’s poetry, which stands on its own merit, can also be read in relation to Wuthering Heights. Although details concerning the inception and the production of the novel are scant, several accounts have been written, including the one cited below.
